completed_bricks.notes: Phone test passed: real phone -> Telegram -> Render -> engine -> Telegram -> real phone. Webhook registered at https://omni-kzdn.onrender.com/telegram/webhook. Deployment live on Render free tier; cold start ~30s after 15 min idle.

open_risks: OpenRouter free-tier model slugs rotate; default may need updating via OPENROUTER_MODEL env var over time
Routing (S4) selects logical names but every name resolves to one concrete model per provider (D007); physical per-tier model differentiation needs a second registered model
Retry (S5) is complete but a live fallback (MODEL_FALLBACK) only changes the outcome once it resolves to a different provider/model than the primary (D008)
Milestone C uses forward-only SQL migrations against real Postgres - the deploy-safety surface; no destructive/down migrations

ConstitutionRepository's _next_version reads MAX + inserts in two statements (no row lock). Safe at single-operator scale; a concurrent-writer retry-on-UNIQUE-violation lands at Milestone F when workers exist.

Milestone D is synchronous (D016): the Telegram webhook handler calls the model inline. Telegram retries on timeout (~seconds), so a slow model call risks duplicate replies. Async/background execution is Milestone F. Acceptable for D's definition of done; noted so it isn't mistaken for a bug.

Webhook handler replies do NOT cover model-error or send-error cases (D4 stays silent and logs). If the phone test at D5 appears to 'hang' with no reply, check the app logs before assuming the bot is dead.
Render free tier sleeps after 15 minutes idle; the first request after wake takes ~30s. Acceptable for single-operator use; a Milestone E/F concern if async replies make latency matter more.

Webhook URL is not idempotent across Telegram retries: if a model call exceeds Telegram's ~seconds timeout, the same update_id can produce a duplicate reply. Milestone F's job queue is the fix; noted so a future duplicate-reply report is diagnosed as known.
